extended_summary: PowerMateManager.swift serves as the central orchestration layer and gesture engine for the PowerMate hardware integration system. It implements the PowerMateTransportDelegate protocol to receive raw button and rotation events from multiple concurrent transports (USB HID and BLE), then applies temporal logic to detect high-level gestures including single presses, double taps, and long presses. The class maintains unified LED state across all transports and acts as the sole intermediary between low-level hardware drivers and the AppDelegate's user-facing mode management. Its gesture detection implementation uses Timer-based state machines with configurable thresholds, tracking button-down timing, tap counting, and rotation-during-press detection to disambiguate user intent.

decision_chains.decision: Pure userspace IOKit HID instead of kernel extension
decision_chains.rationale: The document explicitly states this enables macOS 13+ compatibility without requiring privileged kernel code, reducing deployment friction and security review burden.
decision_chains.tradeoffs: May limit low-level hardware access or latency guarantees compared to kext approach; some advanced HID features may be unavailable in userspace.

decision_chains.decision: Four-mode architecture with long-press cycling
decision_chains.rationale: A single physical knob must control multiple domains (volume, brightness, MIDI, custom profiles); gesture-based mode switching maximizes control density without additional UI chrome.
decision_chains.tradeoffs: Mode cycling adds cognitive load; users must remember current mode; long-press timing must be tuned to avoid accidental triggers during normal rotation.

decision_chains.decision: DDC/CI + gamma hybrid for brightness control
decision_chains.rationale: Gamma adjustments provide immediate visual feedback matching knob rotation speed, while DDC/CI hardware changes apply asynchronously in background for persistence.
decision_chains.tradeoffs: Gamma is non-persistent and affects color accuracy; DDC/CI is unreliable on some monitors and requires IOKit privileges; two-path system increases implementation complexity.

decision_chains.decision: Custom mode engine with per-app profiles and extended press sustain
decision_chains.rationale: NSWorkspace frontmost-app observation enables context-aware behavior where the knob adapts to active application; extended press (hold-to-sustain) enables continuous actions like scrubbing or sustained notes.
decision_chains.tradeoffs: Profile management adds state complexity; extended press disables mode cycling, creating modal interaction that may confuse users; per-app configuration requires maintenance as applications update.

decision_chains.decision: LED follows current mode's value in real time
decision_chains.rationale: Visual feedback on the physical device itself bridges the gap between screen state and hardware, especially important when mode cycling obscures which domain is active.
decision_chains.tradeoffs: Requires continuous HID write traffic; LED brightness may not map linearly to perceived value; adds power consumption and potential USB bandwidth contention.

decision_chains.decision: Use seven-tier fallback chain for volume control instead of single API
decision_chains.rationale: Different macOS audio device types have radically different volume capabilities—HDMI/DP have no software volume, Bluetooth has transport-level volume, pro audio interfaces disable OS volume. A single approach cannot cover all scenarios.
decision_chains.tradeoffs: Increased implementation complexity and maintenance burden; requires robust device detection and routing engine.

decision_chains.decision: Prioritize CoreAudio VirtualMasterVolume (Tier 1b) before AppleScript fallback
decision_chains.rationale: VirtualMasterVolume is what macOS's own volume slider uses, has <1ms latency vs 10-50ms for AppleScript, broader device coverage than raw VolumeScalar, and avoids expensive process spawn on every knob tick.
decision_chains.tradeoffs: Requires AudioToolbox framework and proper use of AudioHardwareService APIs; returns kAudioHardwareUnknownPropertyError for truly volume-less devices.

decision_chains.decision: Defer HAL proxy plugin (Tier 5) to v2.0 and DDC/CI (Tier 4) to v1.2
decision_chains.rationale: HAL plugin requires admin installation, coreaudiod restart, and significant development effort (weeks). DDC/CI has monitor compatibility issues and rate limiting constraints. CoreAudio improvements provide immediate value for majority of devices.
decision_chains.tradeoffs: Users with HDMI-only setups (no DDC/CI monitors) will lack volume control until v2.0; media keys remain coarse last resort.

decision_chains.decision: Distribute outside Mac App Store with notarization
decision_chains.rationale: Sandbox and hardened runtime restrictions prevent HAL plugin installation, DDC/CI IOKit access, and some CoreAudio operations required for full functionality.
decision_chains.tradeoffs: Loses App Store discoverability and automatic updates; requires manual distribution infrastructure.

decision_chains.decision: Use device UID (not name or AudioDeviceID) for persistent device identification
decision_chains.rationale: AudioDeviceIDs change between reboots; identical devices have same names but different UIDs. Prevents state corruption when multiple identical USB headsets are connected.
decision_chains.tradeoffs: UIDs can still change for some Bluetooth devices after sleep/wake reconnection; requires additional re-detection logic.

extended_summary: This document is a comprehensive research and strategy guide for implementing industrial-strength macOS system-level volume control in PowerMateReborn, a native Swift menu bar application for Griffin PowerMate USB/Bluetooth controllers. It details a seven-tier fallback architecture (CoreAudio direct, virtual master, AppleScript, simulated media keys, DDC/CI, HAL proxy plugin, and DriverKit), extensive device taxonomy by transport type, capability detection algorithms, and a phased implementation plan (v1.1–v2.0). The document is highly active and current (last updated March 2026), with explicit task priorities, open research questions, and direct relevance to ongoing development. It serves as the technical foundation for the audio control subsystem, bridging hardware integration challenges with macOS audio architecture constraints.

decision_chains.decision: Use tiered fallback chain: DisplayServices → CoreDisplay → DDC/CI → Gamma → Overlay
decision_chains.rationale: The document establishes that no single method works for all display types on macOS. Apple displays need DisplayServices, third-party externals need DDC/CI for true hardware brightness, DisplayLink needs overlay, and gamma serves as universal software fallback. This maximizes compatibility coverage.
decision_chains.tradeoffs: Increased implementation complexity and maintenance burden versus single-method approaches; overlay method has screenshot/recording artifacts that gamma avoids

decision_chains.decision: Implement hybrid DDC+gamma feedback for knob rotation
decision_chains.rationale: DDC/CI commands have 50-200ms latency due to slow I2C bus, which would make knob rotation feel sluggish. Gamma table updates are sub-millisecond and provide immediate visual feedback while DDC hardware changes queue and catch up.
decision_chains.tradeoffs: Brief period where displayed brightness doesn't match actual backlight level; potential visual inconsistency if DDC command fails after gamma already applied

decision_chains.decision: Target frontmost display (mouse cursor location) as default control target
decision_chains.rationale: Most intuitive for multi-monitor setups where user expects to control the display they're currently working on. CGMainDisplayID() would always target primary display regardless of user focus.
decision_chains.tradeoffs: Requires continuous mouse position polling or event listening; user may accidentally change wrong display if mouse strays; adds complexity over single-display targeting

decision_chains.decision: Defer Metal shader post-processing (Tier 7) to future v3.0+
decision_chains.rationale: Gamma tables are simpler, sufficient for current needs, and well-documented. Metal approach avoids gamma conflicts with Night Shift/f.lux but requires complex GPU pipeline implementation with uncertain performance implications.
decision_chains.tradeoffs: Gamma table conflicts with other gamma-modifying apps remain unaddressed in near term; Metal would offer more sophisticated tone mapping and HDR handling

decision_chains.decision: Use AppleSiliconDDC library rather than building custom DDC implementation
decision_chains.rationale: The library by @waydabber (BetterDisplay author) is the definitive open-source solution for Apple Silicon DDC, handles both USB-C/DP and HDMI paths, and is already used by MonitorControl and BetterDisplay. Building custom would require deep IOKit expertise and extensive hardware testing.
decision_chains.tradeoffs: Open-source version may lack M1 HDMI-specific fixes present in BetterDisplay's closed-source version; dependency on external project maintenance and licensing compatibility

extended_summary: This document is a comprehensive research and design specification for macOS display brightness control strategies in the PowerMateReborn project. It details a seven-tier fallback architecture (DisplayServices → CoreDisplay → DDC/CI → Gamma tables → Overlay dimming → Simulated keys → Metal shaders) for controlling brightness across all display types including Apple-built-in, third-party external via various connections, and DisplayLink virtual displays. The document serves as the technical foundation for implementing hardware knob-based brightness control, with particular focus on the user's target configuration of Mac Studio + LG HDR 4K over HDMI. It contains detailed implementation plans across three phases (v1.1 gamma fallback, v1.2 DDC/CI hardware control, v1.3+ polish), extensive edge case analysis, and competitive landscape research. The document is actively referenced by the project README and represents current strategic planning as of March 2025.

extended_summary: This is a Sparkle framework appcast XML template that serves as the canonical reference for structuring RSS feed entries for PowerMateReborn's auto-update mechanism. It defines the required XML namespace declarations, channel metadata, and a placeholder <item> block with all necessary Sparkle-specific elements including version numbering (both sparkle:version for internal build numbers and sparkle:shortVersionString for user-facing versions), minimum system version requirements, and an enclosure with EdDSA signature placeholder for secure update verification. The template is designed to be copied and populated for each new release, with explicit REPLACE_WITH_* markers indicating manual steps in the release process.
